data.abstract: Manual evaluation of handwritten answer sheets is often time-consuming, error-prone, and subject to human bias. This paper presents a novel AI-driven framework for automating the evaluation of handwritten descriptive answer scripts using a combination of Optical Character Recognition (OCR), Natural Language Processing (NLP), and Deep Learning. The proposed system first digitizes handwritten scripts using high-resolution scanning, followed by accurate text extraction with OCR. The extracted text is then analyzed using NLP techniques—such as tokenization, POS tagging, and named entity recognition—to understand the semantic structure and context of responses. A deep learning model based on Convolutional Recurrent Neural Networks (CRNN) further refines the evaluation process by assessing content relevance against predefined keywords and patterns. The system ensures a more objective, scalable, and efficient grading process. By integrating computer vision with advanced language models, this approach significantly reduces examiner workload, enhances grading fairness, and opens new avenues for intelligent educational assessment.

data.title: A Unified Deep Learning Framework for Context-Preserving Text Data Cleaning in Multilingual Environments

data.abstract: The insanity of the multilingual and user-generated text information sources is a growing subject of social media, customers reviews, and international communication systems that poses a considerable challenge to automated data cleaning. Conventional preprocessing methods fail to address ambiguity, polysemy, code switching and loss of contextual meaning with resulting poor performance in subsequent natural language processing (NLP) applications. The suggested paper will introduce a new deep learning model, MTC2A-Transformer (Multilingual Transformer with Context-Aware Autoencoder), that will help to overcome these issues in a single form. The model combines a multilingual transformer encoder to produce contextsensitive embeddings, which reflect semantic subtleties in multiple languages with a context-sensitive denoising autoencoder that recovers clean, semantically intact text. Also, a dual attention process aligns cross-lingual and intra-lingual relationships between tokens, and the problem of polysemy and code-switched text is practically resolved with the preservation of sentencelevel meaning. Evaluation on the multilingual and code-switched data collected experimentally shows that the suggested solution can provide a significantly better quality of cleaned text than traditional rule-based methods and single-language deep learning techniques. The MTCA-Transformer model offers a language independent, context aware, and scalable text data cleaning mechanism, which allows more robust downstream NLP algorithms to be applied, sentiment analysis, information retrieval, and machine translation. This paper shows how hybrid transformerautoencoder systems can be used to further the development of automated multilingual text preprocessing.

data.abstract: A linguistic expression, Sarcasm generally conveys the opposite meaning of what had been said in words, which makes it a compplex process for the machines to find out the real meaning. It is mainly depends on the context, making it hard for computation task and is largely defined by the inflexion with which it is spoken, with suggestion of irony. Furthermore, sarcasm express the negative sentiments using positive word, enabling it to confuse sentiment analysis (SA) model. Sarcasm detection is a crucial challenge in natural language processing (NLP), which is required for good understanding to serve as an interface for mutual interaction between humans and machines. This article develops an Enhanced Sarcasm Detection using Grey Wolf Optimizer with Deep Learning (ESD-GWODL) technique on social media. The major intention of the ESD-GWODL method is to detect and classify sarcasm on social media. To accomplish this, the ESD-GWODL technique applies data pre-processing to transform the input data into relevant format. Besides, TF-IDF model can be used to extract word embedding. To detect and categorize sarcastic texts, the ESD-GWODL technique applies long short-term memory (LSTM) model. The ESD-GWODL technique utilizes GWO algorithm for hyperparameter tuning purposes in order to boost the sarcastic text detection. The experimental evaluation of the ESD-GWODL technique is tested using sarcasm dataset. The obtained values infer that the ESD-GWODL technique has resulted in boosted detection results.
